approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of the 64 best molecules actually evaluated in the current session. It draws parents from score quantiles, makes fresh candidates with single-cut fragment crossover or ordinary atom/bond edits, and optionally edits a crossover product once more. Stable molecular identity, novelty and an existing source-relative sulfur rule govern admission. A Gaussian process over count-Morgan fingerprints uses all accepted observations to select ten molecules from each 160-member pool with correlated posterior draws. After three batches without improvement, eligibility is restricted to the forty highest posterior means. Accepted offspring update both the model archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Replace the single-cut crossover constructor with one directed SELFIES path between the same two selected parents. Successive token replacements move toward the second parent's encoding; choose the nonparent intermediate with the strongest balanced structural similarity to both. Earlier trials used arbitrary one-token mutation or chemically typed single-cut joins, while crossover removal lost useful progress. This proposal conditions every replacement on the actual partner and selects within that one path. It changes crossover construction while retaining ordinary mutation, population selection and posterior allocation.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is weak conversion of late proposal effort into large useful alternatives. On actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, the three published Search summaries and run.log files are successful, with complete mean 0.607030316211131 and population SD 0.030175277546149237. Independent joins of its fifteen task logs to their trajectories reproduce 435 full pools, 4350 accepted optimizer purchases, 1480 crossover purchases (476 with successful finishing), 634 strict best-generating-parent wins and positive source-margin mass 16.891241376231875. Late optimizer ordinals 146..290 contain 2175 purchases but only 76 incumbent improvements and incumbent gain mass 1.0224077547621127, versus 253 and 5.978073077532332 over the full panel. The Parent analysis also records concentration on substituted scaffolds; this is a proposal limitation hypothesis, not proof that crossover alone causes it. Current-Parent route removal n-060debe936b2 eliminates recombinant purchases and loses 0.051489597325333, so route removal is not this intervention. Random one-token SELFIES n-700f8a4cd559 and typed single-cut crossover n-55d120396e72 have correctly exposed construction but losses 0.127509460790014 and 0.09479254157802065 against their own earlier code Parent n-1744a1494180 (mean 0.59645311428869), not against the current Parent. Their analyses record fewer useful gains despite broader reach or more local wins. Directed two-parent interpolation is a specific different construction, with no claim that these adverse recipes become useful. Exact read inputs, hashes, signed historical endpoint cells and Parent measurements are in policy/scratch/r0071-02-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json and the fifteen exact per-cell audit paths listed in that manifest; the original analyses are nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/analysis.json, nodes/n-060debe936b2/analysis.json, nodes/n-700f8a4cd559/analysis.json and nodes/n-55d120396e72/analysis.json.

literature_review.conclusion: Adopt only directed two-parent path construction and balanced structural ranking, with the explicitly bounded isomeric/count-kernel adaptations. The scientific reason is internal: current crossover removal loses larger progress, while random token edits and locally typed grafts are exposed adverse constructions. These facts motivate a distinct, fixed construction test, not assumed paper-to-campaign efficacy, restored source-subgraph conservation, extra development allowance or permission to retune a refuted recipe. Exact activation and real endpoint utility remain separate future measurements.

method_change.previous_method: The actual n-cf8d309c06de GraphOperators.crossover chooses one cut fragment from each accepted graph and joins the retained core and graft with a single bond.
method_change.proposed_method: One directed SELFIES path between the same ordered accepted parents, selecting the first nonparent intermediate maximizing balanced count-Morgan similarity.
method_change.rationale: Current-Parent crossover removal loses complete utility, while the historical typed constructor and arbitrary-token mutation have correct exposure but poorer useful gains. Endpoint-conditioned interpolation tests a specific different source of structural alternatives without changing ordinary mutation, admission, feedback, population or acquisition.

hypothesis: Change only the crossover construction law from a single-cut graph graft to a directed, parent-conditioned SELFIES interpolation path. For the same ordered pair of accepted parents, independently permute each atom order once with the existing session RNG, encode the two exact isomeric source views, right-pad the shorter token list with a removable blank, shuffle the differing positions once, and replace each position by the second parent's actual token. Decode the successive path states. Among valid canonical-unique intermediates distinct from both exact parents, return the first path-position maximizer of F=(s_first+s_second)/2-abs(s_first-s_second), where s uses the Parent's unchanged radius-2, 2048-dimensional chirality-aware count-Morgan generalized Tanimoto. The causal path is endpoint-conditioned token construction -> a nonparent intermediate resembling both real sources -> unchanged admission, finishing, posterior purchase and real feedback -> potentially larger endpoint gain. Token mismatch strictly decreases; molecular similarity, source-subgraph preservation, chemical utility and score need not increase. One path is the entire constructor support per call; there is no arbitrary alphabet draw, mutation-neighborhood replacement or new acquisition reward.

finding_summary.headline: Directed paths reached every session, but smaller gains and lower final scores refute the promised benefit
finding_summary.insights:
The two borrowed elements—endpoint-directed token interpolation and balanced two-parent similarity choice—both operated under the declared one-path, exact-identity and count-fingerprint adaptations. Their failure here is a failure to deliver the promised endpoint benefit, not evidence that the code never used them. It does not reproduce or settle the published methods with multiple paths and different similarity conventions.

The loss cannot be explained merely by more tiny fragments or less overall scaffold variety. Purchases below twelve heavy atoms fell from 124 to one, those above sixty fell from 21 to zero, and typed/generic scaffold coverage rose from 1,667/951 to 2,296/1,303. Even after excluding small fragments, within-session fingerprint similarity fell from 0.630 to 0.593. Broader structures and resemblance to both parents were therefore insufficient to produce larger gains. The search still drew on recent ancestry: the oldest generating parent averaged 2.84 batches old, versus 2.89 in the Parent, and one session placed all 29 of its upper-decile purchases on one typed scaffold. The observed limitation concerns constructing and retaining several productive core families, capabilities that structure-preserving proposal operators or population schemes maintaining multiple core families could supply. Their benefit remains untested.

The molecular assessment shows that broader topology also brought more large-ring structures and cumulated double-bond arrangements. N-halogen and peroxide liabilities persisted, and defined stereochemistry remained absent. Carbonyls, amides and ring amines are present; narrow aromatic-excluding SMARTS must not be mistaken for missing functional groups. These associations do not prove that any liability caused the score loss or justify a new chemical filter. The experiment also cannot separate the effects of source certification, path ranking, finishing, posterior selection and changed adaptive history. It settles the fixed proposal’s benefit prediction while leaving the broader recombination approach open.
finding_summary.results:
The constructor ran as registered in all fifteen sessions. Independent replay verified 32,118 complete directed paths from 33,808 crossover requests; 1,690 requests failed the specified source-identity certification and nine had no nonparent intermediate. The paths supplied 1,306 real purchases, all with positive fingerprint similarity to both original parents. Of these, 1,009 were the chosen immediate product and 297 were changed by finishing edits. Their feedback reached the next fit for 1,261 purchases; 45 were in the final batch and therefore had no later fit. A total of 672 path products were later used as actual breeding parents, with 3,807 session-unique accepted transitive descendants. These ancestry counts show delivery, not isolated causal mediation.

The optimizer made more full-panel parent-beating purchases, 660 versus 634, but their total positive gain fell from 16.891241 to 13.582221. On the final 145 purchases of each session, the corresponding gain fell from 4.402370 to 3.432685. Total sequential incumbent gain also fell, from 5.978073 to 4.921175 overall and from 1.022408 to 0.845792 late. The original crossover route produced 1,480 purchases and 5.679911 total positive parent gain; the path route produced 1,306 and 3.855365.

Every session completed its full budget. Mean final score fell from 0.607030 to 0.536570, a paired change of -0.070460 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed changes were -0.144589, -0.039528 and -0.027262; twelve of fifteen task/seed endpoints and all five task means were lower. The registered useful-recombination prediction is therefore refuted despite correct construction, real exposure and later reuse.

molecular.headline: Medium-sized, ring-rich molecules with broader scaffold coverage, but unresolved stereochemistry and frequent strained or reactive motifs
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-be5eab357d90 against its actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, using only the frozen Search panel 0/1/2. The request separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; all fifteen Child and fifteen Parent trajectories were present and read. Each supplies 300 accepted observations per session, including ten initial observations. All chemistry counts below concern the 4,350 accepted optimizer proposals per node, not unscored construction intermediates or candidate pools. Score-defined upper/lower deciles mean 29 of 290 optimizer records within each session, combined to 87 per task; existing scores are used without any new scoring. The Child produces mainly medium-sized aryl/heteroaryl compounds, N-heterocycles, amides or lactams, ethers, sulfonamides and sulfur-containing variants. RDKit perception finds rings in 4,349 and aromatic atoms in 4,302 proposals. Heavy-atom min/p10/median/p90/max is 5/25/30/36/43, versus 1/24/28/34/96 in the Parent. Only one Child proposal is below twelve heavy atoms and none exceeds sixty, versus 124 and 21 in the Parent; the old near-single-atom tail is therefore not a current dominant gap. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 2,296/1,303 among 4,349 scaffold-bearing Child records, versus 1,667/951 among 4,255 Parent records. Empty scaffolds are one versus 95; extraction failures are zero for both. These pooled counts describe broad constitutional exploration, while the higher-scoring subsets can remain narrow. Chemical quality is mixed. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with 699 N-halogen, 111 O-halogen and 118 peroxide-bearing Child molecules. There are 409 molecules with a carbon carrying cumulated double bonds versus five in the Parent, and 1,279 with an RDKit-perceived ring of at least eight atoms versus 453. Small all-aromatic ring and small unsaturated ring flags occur in 252 and 823 Child records versus 170 and 672 Parent records. These flags warrant structural inspection; neither ring size nor unsaturation alone proves impossibility. The topological breadth does not establish synthetic accessibility, stability or pharmacological utility. No Child proposal has specified atom or double-bond stereochemistry, although 2,755 have an unassigned stereocentre. All have zero total formal charge and zero radical electrons; two contain internally charge-separated N=N groups, so absence of all charged atoms would be an incorrect claim. The Parent likewise has no specified stereochemistry or radicals. Provenance: the original immutable request is policy/requests/r0071-02-improve-L01-molecular-assess-64136e09830b46b5.json; the scheduler refresh is policy/requests/r0071-02-improve-L01-molecular-assess-2844152be4fdf989.json. Their molecular digest, citation trajectories, comparison, ticket, intent hash and stage profile are identical. Child evidence remains in the exact request-authorized outside-run slot staging paths cited per task; no published Child archive exists at assessment time. That publication gap is not missing Search chemistry and is not replaced by an invented future archive citation. Parent evidence is its indexed published Search archive. All input files, SHA256 hashes, cohort definitions and derived counts are recorded in policy/scratch/r0071-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and the per-task audits. Functional-group statements use the aromatic-inclusive supplement policy/scratch/r0071-02-improve-L01/molecular/functional-group-interpretation.json: the earlier audit fields defined by [C]=[O] and [CX3](=O)[NX3] are narrow SMARTS counts and must not be mistaken for total carbonyl/amide coverage. Existing audit bytes are preserved. Comparisons describe chemistry associations on this panel; they do not establish activation, component attribution, an unobserved target pharmacophore, or a benefit from any suggested change.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer molecules have 16-28 heavy atoms, median 25, and median three rings/two aromatic rings. The seed-0 high-scoring family retains a substituted indole carboxanilide with amino, methoxy and halogen-bearing side groups. Seed 1 instead uses a partially unsaturated N-containing seven-membered ring, a halophenyl group, an enamine-like side chain and an alkynyl alcohol. Seed 2 expands the indole-associated carbocycle to an eight-membered unsaturated ring with an allene, methoxy and vinyl groups, while retaining a pyridyl carboxamide. The final seed-2 molecule replaces part of that ring by a sulfur-containing nine-membered ring. There are 436 typed and 167 generic scaffolds versus 186 and 69 in the Parent, but fewer aromatic rings at the median, two versus three. Aromatic carboxamides are recognizable synthetic motifs; the allene-containing rings, N-halogen substituents and bromomethyl ether-like group make much of this particular output questionable as a set of stable, readily made compounds. liabilities: There are 85 cumulated-carbon, 216 N-halogen and ten peroxide-bearing proposals. An eight-membered cyclic allene and extended conjugated/enamine systems require geometry and stability assessment beyond a valid SMILES.

The highest-scoring expanded-ring compound still leaves substituent stereochemistry unspecified; 237 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre. The seed-0 bromomethyl ether-like substituent and seed-1 N-chloro/N-fluoro groups add potentially reactive functionality.
missing_features: The output does not show a broad set of conventional, geometry-defined alternatives around the better-scoring aryl/polar architectures. Large unsaturated-ring and enamine families replace much of the compact aromatic-amide coverage; the observed exceptions prevent claiming that one exact amide or heteroaryl motif is mandatory.

Stereochemical definition and differentiated ionic states are essentially unrepresented. The two internally charge-separated N=N examples are exceptions to atomwise neutrality, not an explored series of defined protomers. Their existence does not demonstrate a score advantage for charge or stereochemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The highest observed Child molecule is the expanded-ring pyridyl carboxamide at 0.44320263021395917, versus 0.00034958375642754933 for the much smaller fluorinated trimethoxyindole that lacks the carboxamide and second aryl ring. The shared initial trimethoxyindole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Retaining connected aromatic/polar architecture is associated with the stronger sampled values, but is not a universal requirement: the seed-1 carbonyl-free family reaches 0.40497388700123543. Two otherwise matched pyridyl F/Br variants tie at 0.4064863843781577, so those substitutions provide no visible gradient. The Child upper deciles contain 44 amide/lactam-bearing records of 87, versus 87 of 87 in the Parent, and 36 typed/19 generic scaffolds versus 11/5. Parent leaders retain compact aromatic carboxamides and also include N-halogen liabilities; the Child has not simply supplied more conventional versions of the same chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals span 5-41 heavy atoms with median 32 and median four rings/three aromatic rings. High-scoring seed-0 structures are densely connected N/O/S heterocycles with imine-linked fluoroalkyl substituents, carbonyl/thione groups and very small fused rings; the best has 37 heavy atoms and nine RDKit SSSR rings. Seed 1 instead reaches a linked N-rich heteroaryl series with an aminal-like centre, haloalkyl groups and sulfur-halogen functionality. Seed 2 favors an amino sulfur-containing heterobicycle, a substituted aza-aromatic group and branched fluoroalkoxy side chain. The final seed-2 compound also carries an O-Cl bond. These are ring-rich, heavily decorated structures, not simple scaffold-free fragments. Whole-molecule synthetic plausibility is questionable, especially for the compressed fused topology and the labile heteroatom-halogen groups. liabilities: Small all-aromatic ring flags occur in 234 of 870 Child proposals versus 85 in the Parent; small unsaturated rings occur in 252. The highest seed-0 family contains tightly compressed O/S-containing ring fusions whose feasibility is not established by sanitization.

There are 169 N-halogen and 51 O-halogen proposals, alongside aminal-like links, imines and sulfur-halogen bonds. The isolated low-score N-fluoro fragment shows that fragmentary reactive species have not disappeared completely.
Of 870 proposals, 425 have unassigned stereocentres and none specifies stereochemistry.
missing_features: The favorable score region is represented by few constitutional families, especially one typed scaffold throughout the seed-2 upper decile. The sampled chemistry lacks broad alternative compact heteroaromatic arrangements with comparable polar-group placement; no specific unseen decoration can be inferred from these trajectories.
Defined stereoisomers of the branched alkoxy, haloalkyl and aminal-like arrangements are missing. This is an output gap, not evidence that assigning stereo would improve this score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 37-heavy-atom heterocyclic leader scores 0.6215456943011123; the five-heavy-atom N-fluoro fragment scores 0.5013169446883231, and a disrupted polycyclic nonaromatic lactam scores 0.50304960693955. The upper/lower deciles have median heavy-atom counts 34/30 and aromatic-ring counts 3/2. Thus retention of decorated, connected heteroaromatic architecture accompanies higher values in these samples, without showing a unique missing decoration. The upper deciles contain only 15 typed and six generic scaffolds, against 317 and 202 in all Child proposals; every one of the 29 upper-decile seed-2 molecules shares one typed scaffold. Parent seed-0 leaders instead use a more compact fused N-rich oxo/thioxo heterocycle, around 31 heavy atoms and five rings, reaching 0.8561477222467935. Parent leaders also carry O-halogen and other reactive groups, so their larger observed value is not evidence of better chemical quality.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 proposals are halogenated and ring-bearing, with 19-43 heavy atoms, median 34, and median three rings/two aromatic rings. The strongest seed-1 family combines an N-methyl fused aryl/aliphatic amine, an azetidine linker, an amino substituent and a halogenated indane-like group. These molecules contain plausible medicinal-chemistry building blocks, but individual azetine, fused or bridged products require careful geometry assessment. The Child retains sulfonamides in 544 records versus 75 in the Parent and has 479 typed/300 generic scaffolds versus 326/201. This is a chemically different distribution, not absence of ring-bound amines. liabilities: Every one of the 870 Child molecules has at least one unassigned stereocentre; none carries an explicit stereo assignment. The near-unit score therefore does not identify a defined stereoisomer.

There are 238 small-unsaturated-ring flags, and later products can form highly bridged cages. Ordinary saturated azetidines are not inherently implausible, but their unsaturated and multiply bridged relatives require separate scrutiny.

There are 79 peroxide-bearing proposals, predominantly outside the upper deciles, and many retain flexible, heavily heteroatom-substituted sulfur-containing appendages. The score is not a measure of synthesis, stability or selectivity.
missing_features: Basic amine centres and aromatic groups are demonstrably present. What is missing is explicit stereochemical definition of the fused-ring, substituted azetidine and side-chain centres, together with corresponding chemically controlled alternatives to the strained ring variants.

The observed neutral graphs do not explore a documented series of distinct protonation states. The trajectories do not establish which state would be preferred or whether these representations reflect a biologically relevant ionization state.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 aryl/azetidine/indane combination scores 0.9999993170942683. In contrast, an oxygen-rich nonaromatic medium ring lacking nitrogen scores 0.0028675484499697404, and a large acid/amide/sulfonamide initial-architecture derivative scores 0.007860927848215432. A structural proxy for non-amide ring amines is present in 86 of 87 upper-decile records but only 34 of 87 lower-decile records. Upper/lower median sizes are 31/39 heavy atoms; carbonyl-bearing records are 4/69, with no carboxylic acids in the upper group. These associations support connected aryl/basic-amine architectures over the sampled large oxygenated and acid-bearing alternatives; they do not establish a binding mode or pKa. Sulfonamides are not uniformly excluded: 40 upper-decile Child records retain one, whereas the Parent upper deciles contain none. Both nodes reach high-scoring aryl/amine families, and the Parent high series has its own aminal and small-ring liabilities.

There are 136 small-unsaturated-ring flags, 43 O-halogen molecules and 39 phosphorus-containing molecules. None is automatically unmakeable, but the output does not supply a synthetic or stability rationale for these combinations.
Unassigned stereocentres occur in 713 of 870 proposals, with no explicit configurations. Dense carbonyl-rich polycycles and macrocycles leave conformational and stereochemical ambiguity unresolved.
missing_features: The output does not lack carbonyls, amides or aromatic rings. It lacks a well-defined set of less strained alternatives that preserve the higher-scoring relative placement of aryl and N/carbonyl groups while varying the core geometry.

The stereochemical identities of the saturated ring junctions and substituted ring carbons are unspecified. No unsampled target topology or preferred configuration can be deduced from these observed scores.

This is modest diversification within a related chemical envelope, not evidence that more rings or more carbonyls alone improve the objective.

N-halogen bonds occur in 287 proposals, including high-score N-F structures; 179 carry small unsaturated rings. Aldehyde chains, N-S substituents and phosphorus-containing rings add reactivity or synthetic questions not resolved by the score.
Of 870 proposals, 510 have unassigned stereocentres and none specifies stereochemistry. The highest-scoring molecules therefore remain constitutionally defined but stereochemically incomplete.
missing_features: Fluorination, nitrogen heterocycles and carbonyls are present. Missing is broad, chemically conventional coverage of alternative ring/connectivity and oxo/imino arrangements within the favorable composition range; the highest Child series stays tied to a dione, N-F and aldehyde/cyclopropene combination. Imino alternatives exist in another seed, so they must not be described as wholly absent.

Defined stereoisomers and stable alternative presentations of the same heteroatom/halogen content are not demonstrated by these trajectories. The data cannot identify a unique unseen reference motif or justify a task-specific structural recipe.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 cyclopropene/dione leader scores 0.5455448018382273, while a related fused-ring scaffold with a fluoromethyl side chain scores 0.491752401730444. Replacing that side chain by aminomethyl on the same quoted fused-ring skeleton gives 0.0003010877860658217. This observed local pair shows strong sensitivity to substitution and composition; it does not establish a general penalty for amines. An early oxo-rich, nonaromatic polycycle scores 1.1052392081020856e-13. The upper deciles contain halogens in 86 of 87 records, versus 31 of 87 lower records, while all upper records contain carbonyls and 51 have aldehydes. The Parent upper deciles likewise all contain carbonyls but no aldehydes; its leaders emphasize compact fluorinated imino/oxo heterocycles, and a seed-0 example scores 0.7658605860985803. The Child has explored other ring and substituent balances without reproducing that chemistry distribution. Neither those scores nor the aldehyde enrichment establishes desirable stability or biological activity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-be5eab357d90 versus code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and the same accepted-observation conditions: among 4,350 optimizer records per node, cumulated-carbon molecules number 409 versus five, small all-aromatic ring flags 252 versus 170, small unsaturated rings 823 versus 672, and rings of at least eight atoms 1,279 versus 453. These are directly perceived structures with individual high-score witnesses; not every flag is intrinsically unstable. Input hashes and per-cell data are in policy/scratch/r0071-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and its listed immutable audits. The association does not attribute the change to a particular component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output broadens constitutional topology without demonstrating control of strain, bond geometry or preservation of conventional ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs the ability to vary ring topology while tracking the local geometry and chemical character it changes, and to offer conventional alternatives to the same difficult connectivity. Feasibility information would require its own supported validation; these diagnostic flags are not evidence for a universal ring-size cutoff or a proven reward rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-be5eab357d90 on the frozen Search panel, 2,755 of 4,350 accepted optimizer molecules have unassigned stereocentres, while none specifies atom or double-bond stereochemistry. All have zero net formal charge; two carry internal N=N charge separation. The paired Parent also has no specified stereo, so this is an inherited unresolved output limitation, not a newly isolated effect. These counts are in policy/scratch/r0071-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The proposed stereogenic structures lack explicit configurations, and the output scarcely explores distinct ionic forms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to represent and retain explicit configurations when it creates stereogenic centres and distinguish chemically justified ionic forms when applicable. A task-agnostic search could then test those alternatives using current-session feedback. The present trajectories supply no evidence of an enantiomeric, protonation-state or score advantage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The same n-be5eab357d90 Search output contains 699 N-halogen, 111 O-halogen, 118 peroxide and 29 nitroso-bearing molecules. N-halogen bonds remain in high-scoring constitutional families. The paired Parent contains 888, 162, 119 and 242 respectively, so several of these liabilities are less frequent but remain unresolved. The chemistry summary and aromatic-inclusive functional-group supplement preserve the exact source conditions; no synthesis or stability measurements were available.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable functional-group alternatives are not consistently separated from reactive heteroatom-halogen, peroxide and related arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs chemically distinct treatment of carbon halogenation, heteroatom halogenation, oxidation and heteroatom-link formation, together with alternative stable groups it can actually construct. Whether environment-aware edits or additional feasibility information help must be tested separately; their desirability cannot be inferred from a high oracle score or a simple blacklist.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across n-be5eab357d90 there are 2,296 typed and 1,303 generic nonempty scaffolds. In one complete session, all 29 molecules in its score-defined upper decile share one typed scaffold; in another, 27 of 29 share one generic scaffold. The corresponding full pooled task ensemble has 317 typed and 202 generic scaffolds. This is conditional concentration within the frozen Search panel, not global structural collapse. Per-session counts and underlying Child/Parent file hashes are retained in the immutable audits listed by policy/scratch/r0071-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold exploration does not consistently yield multiple chemically distinct families in each session’s higher-scoring output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to sustain and refine alternative core arrangements that retain locally useful chemical relationships, rather than measuring coverage only by the number of distinct scaffolds emitted. Current-session labels can test those alternatives; broader diversity by itself has no demonstrated benefit here, and no component-level explanation follows from this association.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
